I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery.

Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted.

My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable.

When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person.

Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere.
